# TurbineH catalogue

> 158 verified components (licence, security scan and contract tests checked) that TurbineH selects
> for apps. Full machine-readable index: https://software.turbineh.com/catalog/index.json · details per component:
> https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/<id> · CLI: `turbineh search "<need>"`.

- [ai.json-repair.jsonrepair](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.json-repair.jsonrepair): Repairs almost-valid JSON produced by models (missing quotes, trailing commas, code fences). Use when: When model output is syntactically invalid but structurally recognizable Not when: The component does not validate the shape of the repaired value; use a schema validator afterwards — use ai.schema-validation.ajv. Provides ai.json-repair.
- [ai.language-detection.franc-min](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.language-detection.franc-min): Detects the language of a text offline (route to the right prompt or model, label documents). Use when: When you need to detect language offline Not when: Short texts (a few words) are unreliable — use ai.text-chunking.sentence-splitter. Provides ai.language-detection.
- [ai.mcp-server.modelcontextprotocol-sdk](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.mcp-server.modelcontextprotocol-sdk): Exposes the app's own tools and data to AI agents through the Model Context Protocol (server side). Use when: When you need to provide a standardized interface for AI agents to interact with your application's data and tools Not when: Tool permissions and confirmation flows for actions with side effects must be handled by the Safety Pack — use AI Safety Pack. Provides ai.mcp-server.
- [ai.orchestrator.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.orchestrator.turbineh): TurbineH component #001: every AI call of the app is orchestrated — a small open model plans the request, TurbineH orchestration decides the route (which open model), whether it is acceptable and which tool to use, and the chosen open model answers; structured output validated with zod, embeddings for knowledge bases, usage per workspace. Use when: The app needs any language-model call: answers, structured output, embeddings or an agent that acts with tools Not when: No AI is needed: do not add it for deterministic logic (search, rules, calculations). Provides ai.orchestrator.
- [ai.partial-json.partial-json](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.partial-json.partial-json): Parses incomplete JSON while it is still streaming, to show structured results progressively. Use when: When you need to show structured results from a stream before the stream ends Not when: The final value still needs full validation once the stream ends — use ai.schema-validation.ajv. Provides ai.partial-json.
- [ai.prompt-templates.mustache](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.prompt-templates.mustache): Logic-less templates for prompts and messages: values are inserted, never executed. Use when: When you need to inject data into predefined prompt structures Not when: Templates must be written by the app owner, never by end users — use end users writing templates. Provides ai.prompt-templates.
- [ai.schema-validation.ajv](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.schema-validation.ajv): Validates JSON against JSON Schema (structured model output, tool arguments, imported data). Use when: When you need to ensure JSON data conforms to a specific schema Not when: This component does not repair invalid data; it only validates it — use ai.json-repair.jsonrepair. Provides ai.schema-validation.
- [ai.sse-parsing.eventsource-parser](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.sse-parsing.eventsource-parser): Parses Server-Sent Events streams (streamed model answers, progress events). Use when: When you have raw bytes from a fetch response or ReadableStream and need to extract SSE messages Not when: If you need a modern, feature-rich client implementation that manages the connection itself — use eventsource-client. Provides ai.sse-parsing.
- [ai.stopwords.stopword](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.stopwords.stopword): Removes stopwords in many languages for keyword extraction and keyword search. Use when: When you need to strip frequent, low-meaning words from a tokenized array of strings Not when: The component does not perform stemming or lemmatisation — use stemming or lemmatisation. Provides ai.stopwords.
- [ai.text-chunking.sentence-splitter](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.text-chunking.sentence-splitter): Splits text into sentences and size-bounded chunks with overlap for retrieval (RAG) and summaries. Use when: When you need to split text into sentences based on punctuation or language-specific rules Not when: Sizes are measured in characters; count tokens with ai.token-count when exact budgets matter — use ai.token-count.gpt-tokenizer. Provides ai.text-chunking.
- [ai.token-count.gpt-tokenizer](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.token-count.gpt-tokenizer): Counts and truncates text by tokens (BPE) to keep prompts and context within a budget. Use when: When you need to ensure prompts stay within model context limits Not when: If you need to chunk text by sentence boundaries rather than token counts — use ai.text-chunking.sentence-splitter. Provides ai.token-count.
- [ai.vector-store.pgvector](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ai.vector-store.pgvector): Stores and searches embeddings in Postgres with pgvector (Drizzle and SQL helpers), no extra database. Use when: When you already use a Postgres-compatible database (Drizzle, Knex, Prisma, etc.) Not when: If you need a system that also computes the embeddings rather than just storing them — use ai.orchestrator.turbineh. Provides ai.vector-store.
- [auth.mfa.otpauth](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/auth.mfa.otpauth): TOTP/HOTP one-time passwords for two-factor authentication. Use when: When you need to implement RFC 4226 or RFC 6238 compliant one-time passwords Not when: When you require a full session management solution rather than just OTP generation/validation — use auth.session.better-auth. Provides auth.mfa.
- [auth.session.better-auth](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/auth.session.better-auth): Email/password and OAuth authentication with database-backed sessions and cookie handling. Use when: When requiring a comprehensive TypeScript authentication framework with built-in cookie handling Not when: The core package does not implement enterprise SSO (SAML) — use auth.mfa.otpauth. Provides auth.session.
- [authz.organizations.better-auth](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/authz.organizations.better-auth): Organizations (workspaces) with members, roles (owner, admin, member), invitations and an active organization per session. Use when: When your application requires built-in support for organizations and role-based access control within a TypeScript environment Not when: If you only require role management without the organization/workspace abstraction — use authz.roles.turbineh. Provides authz.organizations.
- [authz.roles.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/authz.roles.turbineh): Role policy (owner/admin/member), requireMember guard for every page and server action, requireSession for signed-in non-members and publicAction (per-IP rate limit + Zod) for anonymous visitors. Use when: When requiring role-based access control (owner/admin/member) for entire pages or actions Not when: Does not implement fine-grained per-record permissions — use authz.organizations.better-auth. Provides authz.roles.
- [commerce.cart.zustand](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/commerce.cart.zustand): Small client state store for carts, wizards and UI state. Use when: managing small client-side state collections Not when: Not a database — use a database. Provides commerce.cart.
- [content.frontmatter.gray-matter](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.frontmatter.gray-matter): Parses Markdown files with front matter (title, date, tags) for blogs and pages. Use when: When you need to separate structured metadata from a Markdown body Not when: If you need to render Markdown to HTML — use content.markdown.react-markdown. Provides content.blog.
- [content.html-dom.linkedom](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.html-dom.linkedom): Lightweight server-side DOM to parse and query HTML without a browser. Use when: When you need a lightweight DOM for server-side environments Not when: If you require a different parsing API — use content.html-parse.cheerio. Provides content.html-dom.
- [content.html-parse.cheerio](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.html-parse.cheerio): Parses HTML and extracts data with CSS selectors (structured extraction from pages and emails). Use when: When you need to parse existing HTML strings with jQuery-style syntax Not when: If you require a full DOM implementation — use content.html-dom.linkedom. Provides content.html-parse.
- [content.html-to-markdown.node-html-markdown](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.html-to-markdown.node-html-markdown): Converts HTML to Markdown fast and without a browser DOM (compact context for models, imports). Use when: When high-speed conversion of gigabytes of HTML is required Not when: If you require a full DOM environment — use content.html-dom.linkedom. Provides content.html-to-markdown.
- [content.markdown-to-text.remove-markdown](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.markdown-to-text.remove-markdown): Turns Markdown (e.g. a model answer) into plain text for SMS, notifications or speech. Use when: When you need to remove square brackets, asterisks, and other Markdown syntax from a string Not when: It is not a sanitizer; you must escape or sanitize before rendering as HTML — use content.html-dom.linkedom. Provides content.markdown-to-text.
- [content.markdown.react-markdown](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.markdown.react-markdown): Renders Markdown as React elements without dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Use when: When you need to render Markdown as React elements instead of raw HTML Not when: If you need to use JavaScript and JSX inside your markdown files — use MDX. Provides ui.markdown.
- [content.readability.mozilla-readability](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.readability.mozilla-readability): Extracts the main article content of a web page, dropping navigation, ads and boilerplate. Use when: When you have a DOM document and need to isolate the primary article content Not when: This component requires a DOM document and does not fetch pages itself — use content.html-dom.linkedom. Provides content.readability.
- [content.reading-time.reading-time](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.reading-time.reading-time): Estimates reading time of an article. Use when: When you need a simple word-count based time estimation Not when: The component does not parse Markdown — use content.markdown-to-text.remove-markdown. Provides content.blog.
- [content.rss.feed](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/content.rss.feed): Generates RSS 2.0, Atom and JSON feeds for blogs and news. Use when: When you need to generate structured syndication files from existing content data Not when: This component only generates feeds and does not perform network requests or parsing — use fetching or parsing feeds. Provides content.rss.
- [data.analytics-import.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.analytics-import.turbineh): CSV import for analytics with the columns of the request (date, dimensions such as shop and product, measures such as quantity and revenue): every row validated first and the file imported whole or not at all, with a report of line, column and reason; a dashboard of totals compared with the previous period, measures by day/week/month/quarter/year, top values per dimension and a comparison between values of the scope dimension, filtered by date range and scope value; every chart exported as CSV with the same filters; per-scope access (a shop manager sees and imports only their shop) through record-access.. Use when: The request uploads or imports CSV data and asks for totals, periods, comparisons or charts Not when: Data entered record by record in forms (generated CRUD with a summary page). Provides data.analytics-import.
- [data.countries.i18n-iso-countries](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.countries.i18n-iso-countries): ISO 3166 country codes and localised country names for addresses and shipping. Use when: When you need to map ISO country codes to human-readable names in multiple languages Not when: Does not validate postal addresses — use postal address validation services. Provides data.countries.
- [data.csv-export.csv-stringify](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.csv-export.csv-stringify): Streaming and sync CSV serialisation with quoting. Use when: When you need to serialize data to CSV via streams, callbacks, or synchronous APIs Not when: If you need to parse CSV data instead of generating it — use data.csv-import.papaparse. Provides data.csv-export.
- [data.csv-export.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.csv-export.turbineh): CSV export of workspace-scoped records with spreadsheet formula-injection neutralisation. Use when: When you need to export data to CSV while preventing spreadsheet formula injection Not when: If you require more complex CSV generation features — use data.csv-export.csv-stringify. Provides data.csv-export.
- [data.csv-import.papaparse](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.csv-import.papaparse): Robust CSV parsing with headers, quoting and type detection. Use when: When you need to parse large CSV files without blocking the main thread Not when: Does not validate rows against a schema — use schema validation library. Provides data.csv-import.
- [data.csv-import.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.csv-import.turbineh): CSV import with size and row limits where every row is validated before insert. Use when: When you need to parse CSV data with strict row and byte limits Not when: When you need more advanced parsing features or different dependency profiles — use data.csv-import.papaparse. Provides data.csv-import.
- [data.dates.date-fns](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.dates.date-fns): Pure date arithmetic, comparison and formatting functions. Use when: When performing pure date manipulations without time zone requirements Not when: Does not handle time zones by itself — use date-fns-tz. Provides data.dates.
- [data.dates.dayjs](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.dates.dayjs): Small immutable date library for parsing, arithmetic and formatting. Use when: When a lightweight 2KB alternative to Moment.js is required Not when: If you require a different functional approach or specific feature set provided by date-fns — use data.dates.date-fns. Provides data.dates.
- [data.diff.diff](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.diff.diff): Text and line diffs for change history and reviews. Use when: When you need to identify added or removed lines in a string Not when: The component does not merge conflicting edits — use merging conflicting edits. Provides data.diff.
- [data.duration.ms](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.duration.ms): Converts human-readable durations to milliseconds and back. Use when: When you need to parse or format simple time durations Not when: When you need to handle calendar months or complex date logic — use data.dates.date-fns. Provides data.dates.

Use when: When you need transport/protocol agnostic data fetching (REST, GraphQL, promises) Not when: The library is specifically for managing asynchronous and remote data via hooks — use manual state management. Provides data.fetching.
- [data.fuzzy-search.fuse](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.fuzzy-search.fuse): Client-side fuzzy search over small collections. Use when: When performing client-side searches on small collections Not when: Does not replace database full-text search for large datasets — use database full-text search. Provides data.fuzzy-search.

- [data.ids.cuid2](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/data.ids.cuid2): Collision-resistant, unguessable ids. Use when: When requiring secure, unguessable IDs Not when: High performance tight loops like render loops — use a simple counter. Provides data.ids.

Use when: When lexicographical sort order is required for database indexing or sorting Not when: If you require purely random distribution without encoded time information — use UUID v4. - [deploy.github-pull-request.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/deploy.github-pull-request.turbineh): TurbineH platform service: connect GitHub to a workspace (OAuth with state + PKCE, or a token) and integrate a verified capability package into the client's existing repository as a pull request — adapted to the project's conventions (paths, import alias, existing Drizzle client, package manager), one commit per logical step on turbineh/<capability>, lockfile and migration generated with the project's own tools, then verified inside the project in the sandbox (install, typecheck, lint, tests, capability tests, migration, build); ready for review and state integration_verified only when every check passes, otherwise a draft with the exact failures and next step. Keywords: github, pull request, PR, integrate into existing repo, connect repository, brownfield, add feature to my app, apply to codebase, code review, branch, merge request, monorepo, Next.js, Drizzle, migration, lockfile, verify in project, OAuth, PKCE, CI. Use when: The project is on GitHub, uses Node.js/TypeScript or JavaScript, and the user wants the capability inside it Not when: The project is not on GitHub — use `turbineh apply` (local branch and commit) or the ZIP. Provides deploy.github-pull-request, repo.integration.
- [domain.audit-log.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/domain.audit-log.turbineh): Append-only audit log per workspace: every change made through generated entities and domain components (who, when, action, record, field-level before/after with sensitive values redacted) is recorded by the audit() hook; an owner-visible page with filters (who, action, record type, date range), pagination and CSV export; the database refuses updates and deletes of entries.. Use when: The request says changes are recorded, audited, traceable or visible to owners/admins Not when: Analytics of page views or product events (use an analytics tool). Provides domain.audit-log.
- [domain.bookings.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/domain.bookings.turbineh): Booking domain for any appointment business (clinic, salon, restaurant, studio): team members or rooms, services with duration and price, opening hours per weekday in an IANA time zone (DST-correct), availability computed from real data, create / move / cancel with a notice policy, find bookings by email, double-booking refused by the database, confirmation emails recorded (logged when no provider), staff pages behind an ADMIN_EMAILS allow-list: list, day/week calendar per team member, time off, move and cancel with customer emails; a public booking page (no account) and a cancel link in the confirmation email that honours the notice policy. In AI apps it exposes these operations as a toolkit for runAgent (irreversible ones need the person's confirmation) with a scripted mock model and an E2E suite.. Use when: People book time with a person or a room on fixed opening hours Not when: Ticketed events with seat maps or capacity per slot (one booking per resource per time). Provides domain.bookings.
- [domain.membership-access.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/domain.membership-access.turbineh): Workspace membership from the request: roles and permissions mapped from the spec (owner/editor/viewer, manager/member, staff/client) applied by the one role policy every page and action uses; invitations by email with a role (hashed single-use link, expiry, accept flow for new or existing accounts with requireSession()); role changes and removal that never leave a workspace without an owner; and per-record access scopes (company, project, shop) so restricted members see only their records.. Use when: The request names roles beyond owner/admin/member or says who cannot do what Not when: Single-user apps or staff-only back offices where ADMIN_EMAILS is enough (src/lib/staff.ts). Provides domain.membership-access.
- [domain.workflow.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/domain.workflow.turbineh): Status workflows from the request for any record kind (requests, loans, pieces, tasks): states, initial state, allowed transitions with the roles that may make them (role keys, creator, any member), optional due dates, row-locked state changes, an immutable history of every change with who and when (database-enforced), and alerts for records stuck in a state longer than its limit or overdue; pages per workflow (grouped by state), per record (transitions, history) and an overview of what needs attention.. Use when: The request lists statuses or stages and who may change them Not when: Free-form tags or labels with no order (use a field on the entity). Provides domain.workflow.
- [email.parsing.mailparser](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/email.parsing.mailparser): Parses raw emails (MIME): headers, text, HTML and attachments, for inbox-processing agents. Use when: When processing raw email buffers or strings in Node.js environments Not when: If you only need to convert HTML to plain text — use email.plain-text.html-to-text. Provides email.parsing.
- [email.plain-text.html-to-text](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/email.plain-text.html-to-text): Plain-text version of HTML emails (better deliverability). Use when: When you need to provide a plain-text version of an HTML email to improve deliverability Not when: This component does not send emails — use email.smtp.nodemailer. Not when: If you need a modal dialog instead of a specific input field — use ui.alert-dialog.radix. Provides ui.otp-input.
- [ui.popover.radix](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.popover.radix): Accessible popovers. Use when: When accessibility compliance is required for floating UI Not when: When a modal interruption is required instead of a non-modal popover — use ui.alert-dialog.radix. Provides ui.popover.
- [ui.primitives.react-aria](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.primitives.react-aria): Accessible unstyled components (buttons, fields, dialogs, date fields) from Adobe. Use when: When you need unstyled components that handle complex accessibility and interaction logic Not when: If you prefer pre-styled components from a different primitive library — use ui.checkbox.radix. Provides ui.primitives.
- [ui.primitives.turbineh](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.primitives.turbineh): Accessible UI primitives (button, input, label, card, table) styled with Tailwind. Use when: When building applications requiring accessible base UI components Not when: Does not provide complex widgets such as charts — use ui.charts.recharts. Provides ui.table, ui.form, ui.layout.
- [ui.progress.radix](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.progress.radix): Accessible progress bars (uploads, onboarding). Use when: When accessible progress bars are required Not when: The component is unstyled — use styling-only-approach. Provides ui.progress.
- [ui.scroll-area.radix](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.scroll-area.radix): Custom scroll areas for panels and long lists. Use when: When custom scrollable regions are needed for UI panels Not when: The component is unstyled — use unstyled. Provides ui.scroll-area.
- [ui.select.radix](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.select.radix): Accessible custom select boxes. Use when: When accessibility is a requirement for select components Not when: The component is unstyled — use styling from scratch. Provides ui.select.
- [ui.slider.radix](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.slider.radix): Accessible range sliders (price filters, quantities). Use when: When accessible range selection is required Not when: The component is unstyled — use styling a custom slider from scratch. Provides ui.slider.
- [ui.styling.class-variance-authority](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.styling.class-variance-authority): Typed component variants for utility-class styling. Use when: When building components that require multiple visual states via utility classes Not when: If you require animation logic instead of class composition — use ui.animation.motion. Provides ui.styling.
- [ui.styling.clsx](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.styling.clsx): Builds className strings from conditions. Use when: When you need to build className strings dynamically Not when: If you need to pick colors rather than just join class names — use ui.color-picker.react-colorful. Provides ui.styling.
- [ui.styling.tailwind-merge](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.styling.tailwind-merge): Merges Tailwind CSS classes resolving conflicts (last wins). Use when: When you need to merge Tailwind CSS classes and ensure the last specified utility takes precedence Not when: If you need to select colors rather than merge class strings — use ui.color-picker.react-colorful. Provides ui.styling.
- [ui.switch.radix](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.switch.radix): Accessible on/off switches for settings. Use when: When accessible on/off switches are required for settings Not when: If a checkbox is more appropriate for the selection type — use ui.checkbox.radix. Provides ui.switch.
- [ui.table.tanstack-table](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.table.tanstack-table): Headless table state: sorting, filtering, pagination. Use when: When you need full control over markup and styles Not when: Does not render markup or styles — use ui.accordion.radix. Provides ui.table.
- [ui.tabs.radix](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.tabs.radix): Accessible tabs. Use when: When accessible tab patterns are required Not when: When content should expand vertically instead of switching views — use ui.accordion.radix. Provides ui.tabs.
- [ui.toggle-group.radix](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.toggle-group.radix): Accessible toggle groups (view switchers, filters). Use when: When accessible selection of mutually exclusive or multiple options is required. Not when: When individual independent boolean states are needed rather than a grouped selection — use ui.checkbox.radix. Provides ui.toggle-group.
- [ui.tooltip.radix](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.tooltip.radix): Accessible tooltips. Use when: When accessible tooltip functionality is required Not when: The component is unstyled — use styling-layer. Provides ui.tooltip.
- [ui.url-state.nuqs](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.url-state.nuqs): Type-safe state in the URL query (filters, search, pagination) for Next.js. Use when: When you need type-safe access to search parameters Not when: Not for private data — use local component state. Provides ui.url-state.
- [ui.virtual-list.tanstack-virtual](https://software.turbineh.com/v1/capabilities/ui.virtual-list.tanstack-virtual): Renders very long lists and tables efficiently (virtualisation). Use when: When you need to render large datasets efficiently via virtualization Not when: Does not fetch data — use data fetching logic. Provides ui.virtual-list.
